description.narrative: The overall objective of the intervention is to advance women’s economic empowerment to ensure the capacity of women to participate in, contribute to and benefit from agricultural value chains and processes in ways that affirm the value of their contributions, respect their dignity and promote equality.The project has three specific objectives (SO): SO 1 (personal sphere): To increase women’s agency and decision-making power at household and community level to address barriers to women’s economic empowerment. This specific objective seeks to strengthen women’s capacity, build confidence and self-esteem. SO 2 (relational sphere): To address institutional barriers that limit women’s economic advancement in agricultural value and market chains. This sphere relates to the attitudes and norms of people within women’s lives and the enterprises women may interact with. The objective will work to transform norms, attitudes and values of men, while at the same time support women to develop sustainable and resilient techniques that mitigate the impacts of climate change. SO 3 (social sphere): To strengthen women’s voice and collective power at community level to increase access to, control and ownership of productive (e.g. physical assets, land) and financial assets among women through women-led local organisations, land tenure and financial inclusion. This objective will seek to support the establishment of women-led local organisations, as well as ensuring that women have more access to financial services including insurance and saving groups. Under this objective, the DWAs and women-led local organisations will be trained to lobby and advocate for increased land rights and secure tenure of fertile land.

Projektets övergripande mål är att främja fattiga kvinnors ekonomiska egenmakt för att säkerställa kvinnors förmåga att delta i, bidra till och dra nytta av jordbrukets värdekedjor och processer på sätt som bekräftar värdet av deras bidrag, respekterar deras värdighet, och främjar jämlikhet och rättvisa. Projektet ska genomföras i åtta distrikt i de östra, västra, södra och centrala provinserna i Zambia. Projektet syftar specifikt till att: i) öka kvinnors beslutsfattande på hushållsnivå och samhällsnivå för att hantera hinder för kvinnors ekonomiska egenmakt ii) stärka kvinnors tekniska förmåga att driva och äga livskraftiga, produktiva och hållbara jordbruksföretag och iii) stärka kvinnors röst och kollektiva makt på samhällsnivå för att öka tillgången till, kontrollen av och ägandet av produktiva och finansiella tillgångar för kvinnor, genom stärkta kvinnoledda kooperativ, ökade markrättigheter och ekonomisk inkludering. Detta kommer att uppnås genom en kvinnoledd och kvinnocentrerad strategi, med fokus på både män och kvinnor. Projektet kommer att använda sig av studiecirklar och stödja kvinnogrupper och låneföreningar genom kapacitetsutveckling i ekonomisk egenmakt. Projektet börjar med en åtta månaders inledningsfas, under vilken flera studier kommer att genomföras för att utforma och planera projektet i detalj. En detaljerad arbetsplan kommer också att tas fram under inledningsfasen. Studierna inkluderar marknadsanalys, miljökonsekvensanalys, social konsekvensanalys, analys av konfliktkänslighet, samt en köns- och maktanalys. Resultaten från studierna kommer att ligga till grund för den slutliga utformningen av projektets genomförande. We Effect, Sidas avtalspartner, kommer att genomföra projektet i samarbete med Heifer Project International Zambia (HPIZ), Women for Change (WfC), District Women Associations (DWAs) och Zambia Land Alliance (ZLA). Budgeten för den föreslagna insatsen är 75 miljoner SEK. Projektet kommer att pågå i 44 månader, inklusive inledningsfasen på 8 månader.

The overall objective of the project is to advance women’s economic empowerment to ensure the capacity of women to participate in, contribute to and benefit from agricultural value chains and processes in ways that affirm the value of their contributions, respect their dignity, promote equality and equity in eight districts of Eastern, Western, Southern and Central Provinces of Zambia. Specifically, the project seeks to: i) increase women’s agency and decision-making power at household and community levels to address barriers to women’s economic empowerment. ii) Strengthen technical capacity of women to run and own viable, productive, resilient and sustainable agricultural businesses and iii) Strengthen women’s voice and collective power at community level to increase access to, control of and ownership over productive (e.g. physical assets, land) and financial assets among women through women-led cooperatives, land tenure and financial inclusion.
This will be achieved through a women-led and women­ centred approach with focus on both men and women. In general, the project will work through study circles, and support women groups, village savings and loans associations with capacity building of women in economic empowerment. The project will start with an eight months inception phase during which several studies will be carried out . These include market analysis, environment and social impact assessment, conflict sensitivity analysis, and a gender and power analysis. The findings from the studies will form the basis for the final design of the project implementation.
We Effect, the main agreement partner will implement the project in collaboration with Heifer Project International Zambia (HPIZ), Women for Change (WfC), Zambia Land Alliance (ZLA) and eight District Women Associations (DWAs). The budget for the proposed intervention is SEK 75 Million. The project will run for 44 months including the inception period of 8 months.

description.narrative:
In 2025, the project made steady progress in advancing womens economic empowerment across the targeted provinces. Despite delays linked to the withdrawal of the implementing partner, the project delivered strong results in womens agency, financial inclusion, asset ownership, market access, and climate resilience, with several indicators surpassing their targets.
Under the Overall Objective which is To advance womens economic empowerment by ensuring their ability to participate in, contribute to, and benefit from agricultural value chains in ways that affirm their dignity, recognise their contributions, and promote equality and equity., the following results were noted:
Reduction in Gender Stereotypes: 18,758 women (93%) of the targeted 20,170, reported that gender stereotypes and discriminatory attitudes had reduced within their households and communities, enabling them to participate more freely in economic activities and decision-making processes.
Increased Income: 15,329 women (76%) reported increased income from agricultural enterprises, demonstrating continued engagement in farming and business activities and improved economic opportunities. However, the result fell short of the project target of 85% and represented a decline from the 83% achieved in 2024, suggesting that while a majority of women experienced income gains, factors such as market conditions, climate-related shocks, and economic challenges may have constrained further income growth.
Notable results per specific objectives are as follows:
Specific objective One: To increase womens agency and decision-making power at household and community levels and address barriers to womens economic empowerment.
Key achievements include: Increased Decision-Making Power: 17,145 women (85%) exercised greater influence in household and group decision-making processes, enabling them to take a more active role in economic, agricultural, and family matters and strengthening their agency within households and communities.
Confidence in Managing Money and Businesses: 17,791 women (88.2%) strengthened their confidence and skills in financial management and business operations, enabling them to make informed decisions on budgeting, savings, investments, and enterprise growth. This enhanced their ability to manage businesses, pursue economic opportunities, and contribute meaningfully to household financial decisions.
Access to SRHR and GBV Services:17,899 women and young women (96%) were aware of available Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights (SRHR) and Gender-Based Violence (GBV) services, up from 14,585 in 2024. As a result, 10,636 women (nearly 60%) accessed services including family planning, counselling, testing, treatment, legal support, and GBV case referral and prosecution services, compared to 8,697 women in 2024.
Specific objective Two: Reduce institutional barriers that limit womens economic advancement in agricultural value and market chains.
Key results include: Business Registration: A major institutional achievement was the accreditation of District Women's Development Associations (DWDAs) as PACRA business registration agents, bringing business formalization services closer to women entrepreneurs. Through this mechanism, 1,418 businesses were registered, including 1,374 women-owned enterprises, enabling women to strengthen the legal status of their businesses and improve access to markets, financing, and growth opportunities.
Access to Market Contracts: Market Access and Contracting: 1,210 women (6%) secured individual market contracts, strengthening their access to reliable buyers and formal markets for their agricultural products. In addition, four District Women's Development Associations (50% of the eight DWDAs) collectively negotiated and secured 12 new contracts, creating expanded market opportunities for their members and demonstrating increased capacity to facilitate market linkages and negotiate on behalf of women producers.
Access to Informal Financial Services (VSLAs):15,320 women (76%) increased their incomes through participation in Village Savings and Loan Associations (VSLAs) and other informal financial services, enabling them to strengthen their livelihoods and household economic security. Through their savings groups, women collectively generated ZMW 7,589,711 in share-outs in 2025, demonstrating increased savings capacity and financial resilience. In addition, 7,424 women accessed loans valued at ZMW 6,148,350, which they invested in productive assets, agricultural production, and business expansion, helping to grow their enterprises and income-generating activities
Specific objective Three: To strengthen womens voices and collective power at the community level as well as increase access to, control of and ownership of productive (e.g., physical assets, land) and financial assets among women through women-led cooperatives, land tenure and financial inclusion.
Key achievements include: Access to Formal Financial Services: Women's access to formal financial services continued to improve. In 2025, 43% of targeted women accessed formal financial services, up from 35% in 2024. This included 2,329 women securing Constituency Development Fund (CDF) loans valued at ZMW 3.38 million and 985 women accessing microfinance loans worth ZMW 945,000. Women producers in Mumbwa, Choma, and Lundazi also leveraged additional value-chain financing and crop contracts, bringing the total value of formal financing accessed to approximately ZMW 5 million, including more than ZMW 1 million secured through crop marketing contracts. These investments enabled women to expand agricultural production, invest in productive assets, and strengthen their economic participation in agricultural value chains.
Customary Land Ownership Certificates: 2,308 women obtained Customary Land Holding Certificates in 2025, bringing the cumulative total to 7,849 certificates, close to the project target of 8,100. Notably, 90% of the certificates issued in 2025 were obtained by women using their own resources without project subsidies, demonstrating increased awareness of the benefits of secure land tenure and a strong commitment to protecting their land rights. Through securing land ownership, women strengthened their access to productive assets, enhanced their bargaining power and decision-making authority within households and communities, and actively encouraged other family members to pursue land certification, contributing to wider uptake of land registration.
Specific Objective Four: Increased resilience to environmental and climate change by women, men and youth (male, female)
Key achievements include: Adoption of Climate-Smart Agriculture: Among female farmland owners, 93% adopted at least one climate-smart agricultural practice in 2025. Through conservation agriculture, crop diversification, improved soil management, and water conservation practices, women strengthened their ability to adapt to climate variability, improve farm productivity, and protect their livelihoods from environmental shocks.
Environmental Stewardship: 1,413 households adopted energy-efficient cookstoves, reducing firewood consumption by 40% to 60% and contributing to more sustainable use of natural resources. As a result, women spent less time collecting fuelwood, reduced their exposure to smoke-related health risks, and had more time available for productive and household activities.
Community-Led Conservation: Six DWDAs established and managed community nurseries that produced tree seedlings for planting and restoration activities. Through these nurseries, communities contributed to reforestation efforts, improved soil fertility, and supported biodiversity restoration, strengthening local capacity for environmental conservation and climate resilience.
Yield Indexed Insurance: More than 1,000 of the 12,300 farmers in Mumbwa independently purchased yield-indexed insurance using their own resources in 2025, demonstrating increased confidence in insurance as a climate-risk management tool. This voluntary uptake followed the 2024 pilot, during which 703 insured farmers received drought-related compensation totalling ZMW 356,203, helping farmers to better understand the value of insurance in protecting their agricultural investments and livelihoods against climate shocks.
